title: PIA – Preoperative Intensive Care Monitoring in Acute Stanford Type B Aortic Dissections: Analysis and Evaluation
summary: The primary objective of this study is to assess adherence to current guidelines regarding the initial intensive care management of patients with Stanford type B aortic dissection receiving best medical therapy (BMT) at University Hospital Augsburg. In particular, the study will investigate whether intensive care monitoring with invasive blood pressure measurement and the timing of transfer from the intensive care unit correspond to the guideline-recommended hemodynamic target parameters.  The current guideline does not define a fixed duration of intensive care monitoring but instead relates the duration to the achievement of stable vital parameters (systolic blood pressure of 100–120 mmHg and heart rate ≤60 beats/min). As no systematic data are currently available regarding the duration of intensive care monitoring in clinical practice and its consistency with guideline recommendations, this study will conduct a monocentric analysis of guideline adherence under BMT. Best medical therapy comprises analgesic treatment, particularly opioids such as morphine preparations due to the pronounced pain associated with the condition, as well as antihypertensive treatment, including alpha-1 adrenergic receptor antagonists, calcium channel blockers, beta-blockers, and vasodilators.  The secondary objective of this study is to analyze potential influencing factors and the possible association between the duration of preoperative intensive care monitoring and clinical outcomes. This analysis will be performed for both patients receiving exclusively conservative treatment and patients subsequently undergoing interventional treatment.  The findings may contribute to a critical evaluation of existing therapeutic thresholds and clinical treatment algorithms and, where appropriate, provide a basis for the development of further patient- and disease-course-specific treatment recommendations.  Data will be collected through a retrospective analysis of clinical records, supplemented by questionnaires sent to selected patients.

criteria:
Inclusion criteria:
All patients treated at University Hospital Augsburg between 2017 and 2025 with a Stanford type B aortic dissection will be included. This comprises approximately 270 patients in total.  For selected patients in whom health-related quality of life and psychological burden will additionally be assessed, informed consent to participate in the study must have been obtained after appropriate information has been provided. The same applies to patients or their relatives who are contacted by telephone to assess long-term survival.  Four patient groups of equal size will be selected for the additional assessment of health-related quality of life and psychological burden:  
- Women who attended follow-up appointments 
- Women classified as “lost to follow-up” 
- Men who attended follow-up appointments 
- Men classified as “lost to follow-up”  “Lost to follow-up” is defined as patients whose last documented contact with the hospital, either outpatient or inpatient, occurred more than 12 months previously.
Exclusion criteria:
Patients who were under 18 years of age at the time of aortic dissection.  Patients for whom important previously defined outcome variables are incomplete.
